Java

Writing programs with classes and objects.

What does 'object-oriented' actually mean?

Practise this subject in Blueprint Borough

The basics

  • Getting started with JavaWhat Java is, how a program goes from text to running, and the smallest complete program.
  • Data types and console input and outputThe basic kinds of value in Java, how to read input and print output, and two traps with numbers.
  • OperatorsThe symbols that calculate, compare and combine values, the order they run in, and the difference between == and equals.
  • Control flowHow a program chooses between paths with if and switch, and repeats steps with loops.

Objects

  • Classes, part 1What a class and an object are, and how fields and methods work together.
  • Classes, part 2Constructors, private fields, static members and toString, and why hiding data is a good habit.
  • ArraysHow an array stores a fixed number of values of one type, and how to loop over it safely.

Object-oriented programming

  • InheritanceHow one class can build on another, reuse its code and change what it does.
  • Polymorphism and abstract classesHow one variable can hold many kinds of object and still do the right thing, and how an abstract class sets the rules.
  • InterfacesHow an interface lists what a class can do, without saying how, and why a class can have many.

Real programs

  • Exception handlingWhat happens when something goes wrong while a program runs, and how try, catch and finally deal with it.
  • File handlingHow a program reads from and writes to files, and why try-with-resources closes them for you.
  • GenericsHow type parameters let one class or method work with many types while the compiler checks them.
  • CollectionsThe ready-made lists, sets and maps in Java, and how to choose between them.
